title: Seasonal society jobs: debutantes, Boston Club, Monteleone
summary: Williams describes the yearly round of Christmas, debutante, Mardi Gras and country club jobs played by a ten-piece band, and the move to the Monteleone ballroom.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Every Christmas night we played at the St. Charles Hotel for years. Who was that called? I never know the name of the club, it was some big rich club. But we would start playing from around November the 1st. We would play the introduction nearly to all the debutants at different places, you know. And we'd be playing every night spot job different places from about November the 1st until Mardi Gras night. Mardi Gras day, we'd play at the Boston club, the same job that Celestine had. Mardi Gras day and Mardi Gras night. The Monday before Mardi Gras we played at Boston club. And we had the country club at one time for every Saturday night, 52 Saturday nights. That's right. Then in about January we'd have the T's. They'd have T's from January, the first something till around about the latter part of February. That was two hours from five to seven a T. And we had a large band, ten pieces. Yeah. Right. Right. Right. I just always say now, them fellas should be living today. Look at the money they could be making today, just living today. Yes, indeed. What about that job with Pete?
You say you got Mardi Gras day? Mardi Gras day?

That's at the Mont Leon Hotel. Now I don't know what room, but it's in one of the large rooms. He even had this same job playing for these people about sixteen years. They used to play at the patio royal. But after the crowd got so big, well he had to move over to the Mont Leon Hotel in one of the ballrooms. Which one? I don't know. There's three of them. You don't have any more questions?
